papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: The authors developed a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention to predict gene expression levels from epigenetic modifications across fungal species. The model enables knowledge transfer from well-characterized fungi to less-studied species, helping reveal how epigenetic mechanisms are conserved across phylogenetic distances.

papers.title: Scalable assembly of Ascaris mitogenomes from whole-genome data reveals a novel clade.
papers.abstract: The genus Ascaris is an important group of giant parasitic roundworms, infecting over 700 million people globally and causing substantial economic losses in domestic pigs. Whilst species of Ascaris are morphologically indistinguishable, analysis of mitochondrial loci has revealed three clades (A, B, C) broadly associated with host species and geographic distribution. The diversity within these lineages may expand with the addition of further genomic data. Here, we present a bioinformatic framework for de novo assembly of complete mitochondrial genomes (mitogenomes) from low-coverage whole-geno
papers.summary: The authors developed a bioinformatic pipeline to assemble complete Ascaris mitochondrial genomes directly from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data, enabling mitogenome recovery without targeted enrichment. Applying this to new samples, they uncovered a previously unrecognized clade within the genus, expanding the known mitochondrial diversity of these globally important parasites.

papers.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other a
papers.summary: The authors developed Epi2Hit, a computational method that integrates whole-genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling, and gene expression data to detect biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes via a 'second hit' mechanism: DNA methylation of one allele combined with genomic loss of the other. Applying this to prostate cancer, they identified recurrent epigenetic inactivation events and nominated new putative tumour suppressor genes that would be missed by approaches focused solely on homozygous deletion.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1- patient variant R5179, corresp
papers.summary: This study uses CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying a patient-derived missense variant (R5179) in KMT2D, the gene mutated in Kabuki syndrome type 1. The work addresses the gap that existing KS1 mouse models rely on loss-of-function mutations, while 15-30% of patients carry missense variants. It enables investigation of whether missense variants produce comparable phenotypic features and therapeutic responses.

papers.title: Functional screening of ZIP8 naturally occurring variants identifies pathogenic mutations and trafficking defects.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of human genomic data has revealed a large number of naturally occurring variants, creating a major challenge for functional annotation. The human metal transporter SLC39A8 (ZIP8) is a clinically important divalent metal transporter, yet most of its documented variants remain uncharacterized. Here, we developed a workflow to functionally evaluate ZIP8 variants by integrating laser ablation inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-TOF-MS) with scaled-up cell-based transport assays. Using this method, we systematically analyzed 33 naturally occurrin
papers.summary: The authors developed a workflow combining laser ablation ICP-TOF-MS with scaled-up cell-based transport assays to functionally characterize naturally occurring variants of the metal transporter ZIP8 (SLC39A8). Screening 33 variants, they identified pathogenic mutations and trafficking defects, providing a generalizable approach for annotating variants of clinical importance.

papers.title: Evaluating the pathogenic significance of unique chromosomal variants in craniosynostosis using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and mouse modelling.
papers.abstract: Unravelling causal links between unique structural/copy-number variants (SV/CNV) and associated phenotypes is essential for correct genetic counselling. We investigated two families in which patients with craniosynostosis had SV/CNV potentially dysregulating a fibroblast growth factor (FGF)-encoding gene; a 730 kb dup(4)(q21.21) including FGF5; and a complex 568 kb interspersed 13q12.11 duplication, located 841 kb from FGF9.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: This study investigates two families with craniosynostosis carrying structural or copy-number variants near FGF genes, using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and mouse models to test whether these variants are truly pathogenic. The work demonstrates how functional validation can clarify the causal significance of unique chromosomal variants, which is critical for accurate genetic counseling.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling Primer: Focus on Chromatin and Epigenetics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in modern biology is to understand how molecular interactions produce cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales. Nowhere is this challenge more apparent than in the study of chromatin, where meters of DNA compact into a micron-sized nucleus. How this polymer folds is a dynamic process, regulated by epigenetic modifications-chemical changes to DNA and histones that involve only a handful of atoms. These small changes cooperate to produce emergent, higher-order structures that define cellular identity and function. To explain this system, we must int
papers.summary: This primer reviews multiscale modeling approaches for understanding how chromatin folds within the nucleus and how epigenetic modifications regulate this dynamic process across spatiotemporal scales. It highlights how molecular-level chemical changes to DNA and histones produce emergent higher-order chromatin structures that define cellular identity and function.

papers.title: DNA methylation-based ageing in a deuterostome invertebrate: an epigenetic clock for the crown-of-thorns seastar (Acanthaster cf. solaris).
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable ageing tools are essential for wildlife conservation and management. While DNA methylation has emerged as a promising tool for age estimation in vertebrates, its application to invertebrates remains contested and has been limited to arthropods. Here, we develop an epigenetic clock for the Pacific crown-of-thorns seastar (CoTS; Acanthaster cf. solaris), a destructive coral predator contributing to habitat degradation across Indo-Pacific reefs. Using Oxford Nanopore Technologies, we generated whole-genome DNA methylation profiles across five age groups and identified 1910 C
papers.summary: This study develops the first DNA methylation-based epigenetic clock for an echinoderm, the crown-of-thorns seastar, using Oxford Nanopore whole-genome methylation profiling across five age groups. It identifies 1910 age-associated CpG sites, extending epigenetic ageing tools beyond vertebrates and arthropods to a deuterostome invertebrate. The clock offers a potential conservation and management tool for tracking age structure in this destructive coral predator.

papers.title: Multi-variant GWAS and genomic prediction dissect the genetic architecture underlying tomato fruit weight.
papers.abstract: Tomato fruit weight is primarily controlled by stable genetic effects and domestication-/improvement-associated loci, including prominent chromosome 5 signals, and integrating SNP, INDEL, and SV diversity improves candidate-locus discovery, biological interpretation, and genomic prediction across environments. Tomato fruit weight (fw) is a major breeding target shaped by domestication, crop improvement, and environmental variation. We investigated the genetic architecture and genomic predictability of fw in the Varitome population representing the tomato domestication continuum, including Sola
papers.journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic architecture of tomato fruit weight using multi-variant GWAS that integrates SNPs, INDELs, and structural variants across a population representing the tomato domestication continuum. The authors identify stable genetic effects and domestication-/improvement-associated loci, notably on chromosome 5, and show that incorporating multiple variant types improves candidate-locus discovery, biological interpretation, and genomic prediction across environments.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four widely used prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes, including E. coli, archaea, bacteria, frameshifted genomes, and metagenome-assembled genomes. It provides the first large-scale systematic comparison to guide tool selection for prokaryotic annotation. The results offer practical guidance on tool performance across different genome types and quality levels.

papers.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a genome-wide association meta-analysis and polygenic risk score.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a heritable trait with marked variability in expression and outcomes. Our aims were to discover new genetic loci associated with HCM and to test the effect of a new polygenic risk score (PRS) on incidence, phenotype and outcomes stratified by genotype status.
papers.summary: This study performs a genome-wide association meta-analysis to identify new genetic loci associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and develops a polygenic risk score to predict disease incidence, phenotype, and outcomes. The PRS is tested across different genotype statuses, potentially improving risk stratification beyond monogenic mutations.

papers.title: Development of RS1-specific ACMG/AMP variant classification criteria with pilot variant curation.
papers.abstract: Gene-based therapies are being developed for retinal diseases, including RS1-related X-linked retinoschisis. Therefore it is essential to determine which variants are pathogenic and which are benign when enrolling patients. The Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) X-Linked Inherited Retinal Diseases (XLRD) Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) brings together clinician scientists, molecular biologists, and geneticists to apply their expertise and review the clinical, genetic, population, and functional evidence for variants. American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines have been modifie
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of gene-specific ACMG/AMP variant classification criteria for RS1, the gene implicated in X-linked retinoschisis, by the ClinGen X-Linked Inherited Retinal Diseases Variant Curation Expert Panel. The authors customized the general ACMG/AMP framework with RS1-specific evidence rules and piloted their use by curating a set of variants. This provides a standardized approach for classifying RS1 variants, which is important for patient enrollment in emerging gene therapies.

papers.title: Comparative performance of portable DNA extraction protocols and bioinformatics workflows for rapid detection of gram-negative bacteria and antimicrobial resistance using Oxford Nanopore sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) enables rapid, portable pathogen identification and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) detection, but the reliability of downstream genomic analyses is highly dependent on DNA extraction quality, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study comparatively evaluated four portable bacterial DNA extraction protocols derived from three commercial kits to determine their impact on nanopore sequencing performance, bioinformatics workflow completion, and field deployability. Six gram-negative bacterial isolates (Escherichia coli, n = 4; Pseudomonas sp., n = 1; and
papers.summary: This study compares four portable DNA extraction protocols from three commercial kits for their impact on Oxford Nanopore sequencing performance when detecting gram-negative bacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes. The authors evaluate how extraction quality affects downstream bioinformatics workflow completion and field deployability, using six gram-negative isolates. The work provides practical guidance for choosing extraction methods in resource-limited settings where rapid, portable pathogen detection is needed.

papers.title: Exome sequencing and large-scale analysis of electronic medical record-linked biobank data identify candidate deafness genes.
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in whole-exome sequencing (WES) have enabled large-scale detection of pathogenic variants. Although hundreds of genes are implicated in hearing loss, up to half of inherited cases remain unsolved, limiting eligibility for gene therapy trials that require genetic diagnosis. Biobanks and electronic medical records (EMRs) offer opportunities to integrate genomic and clinical data at scale and expand the spectrum of hearing loss genes. Despite clinical value, EMRs often lack key information such as inheritance patterns, posing challenges for accurate interpretation.
papers.summary: This study combined exome sequencing with electronic medical record-linked biobank data to search for new genes associated with hearing loss, a condition where up to half of inherited cases remain genetically unexplained. By integrating large-scale genomic and clinical data, the authors identified candidate deafness genes, though they note that EMRs often lack key details like inheritance patterns that complicate interpretation.

papers.title: Structural and Thermodynamic Analysis of BRCA1 BRCT Variants Identified in Middle Eastern Breast Cancer Cohorts.
papers.abstract: BRCA1 is a critical tumor suppressor that maintains genomic integrity through its C-terminal BRCT tandem domain, which mediates phosphoprotein interactions involved in DNA damage response signaling. Missense variants within the BRCT domain may disrupt protein stability and phosphopeptide recognition; however, their functional interpretation is often complicated by conflicting computational predictions and limited experimental evidence. We characterized two Middle Eastern BRCA1 BRCT variants, M1652I and F1662S, identified in Bahraini and Lebanese cohorts, respectively and compared their structu
papers.summary: This study structurally and thermodynamically characterizes two BRCA1 BRCT domain variants (M1652I and F1662S) found in Middle Eastern breast cancer cohorts, aiming to clarify their functional impact where computational predictions conflict. The analysis suggests these variants may affect protein stability and phosphopeptide recognition, contributing experimental evidence for variant interpretation in BRCA1-related cancer risk.

papers.title: Characterization of yam virus X isolates from Dioscorea trifida in Brazil.
papers.abstract: Yam virus X (YVX; Potexvirus ecsdioscoreae) is a positive-sense, flexuous RNA virus belonging to the family Alphaflexiviridae. It has been first reported from Guadeloupe, a French archipelago located in the Caribbean Sea. In this study, we investigated the virome in yam (Dioscorea spp.) plant material collected in the state of Bahia (Brazil) by high-throughput sequencing (HTS) on Illumina platform. The objective of the investigation was to explore the occurrence of YVX in yam from South America, and to study its genetic diversity compared to the only one YVX genome sequence available in the Ge
papers.summary: This study used high-throughput sequencing to survey the virome of yam plants collected in Bahia, Brazil, and identified Yam virus X (YVX) isolates infecting Dioscorea trifida. The authors characterized the genetic diversity of these Brazilian isolates relative to the only previously known YVX genome from Guadeloupe, expanding the known geographic and host range of this potexvirus in South America.

papers.title: A Critical Synthesis of Machine Learning in Autism Spectrum Disorder Genomic Research: From Transcriptomics to Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent impairments in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes advances in machine learning applications to ASD genomic research through May 2026, spanning gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing (WES), non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetic profiling, and gut microbiome analysis. A purposive, thematic literature synthesis approach was employed, allowing broad coverage o
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes machine learning applications in autism spectrum disorder genomic research, covering gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing, non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetics, and gut microbiome analysis. It provides a broad thematic overview of how ML methods are being applied across these diverse data types to advance ASD research. The review spans literature through May 2026.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires recognizing sequence-level features across whole bacterial genomes. It addresses the gap left by existing DNA benchmarks, which focus mainly on eukaryotic regulatory elements, and tests whether transformer-based genome models can learn meaningful features beyond those narrow tasks.

papers.title: LDLR Variant Classification Through Activity-Normalized Prime Editing Screening.
papers.abstract: Inherited variants in the LDL (low-density lipoprotein) receptor (LDLR) gene are the most common cause of familial hypercholesterolemia, significantly increasing coronary artery disease risk. Early identification of pathogenic LDLR variants enables prompt lipid-lowering therapy and cascade testing of at-risk relatives; however, most LDLR variants observed in the population have uncertain or absent clinical classifications, leaving many patients without actionable information.
papers.summary: This study uses prime editing to introduce LDLR variants and measures their functional impact on LDL receptor activity, creating a normalized screening approach to classify variants of uncertain significance in familial hypercholesterolemia. By linking measured activity to pathogenicity, the method aims to resolve the many LDLR variants that currently lack clinical classification, enabling earlier diagnosis and cascade testing.

papers.title: metaKEGG: A comprehensive algorithm package to visualize multi-omics pathway enrichment.
papers.abstract: metaKEGG is a comprehensive software package designed to streamline the visualization and integration of pathway enrichment results from multi-omics data, providing accessible and detailed insights into the molecular mechanisms driving health and disease. Unlike standard pipeline approaches, metaKEGG incorporates novel concepts allowing for clear, granular representation of gene-level or transcript-level expression changes. Beyond transcriptomic analysis, metaKEGG also supports epigenetic and regulatory metadata layers, such as methylation profiles and miRNA target annotations, offering users
papers.summary: metaKEGG is a new software package that visualizes and integrates pathway enrichment results across multiple omics layers, including transcriptomic, epigenetic, and regulatory data such as methylation and miRNA targets. It introduces novel concepts for granular gene- or transcript-level representation of expression changes, going beyond standard pathway enrichment pipelines.

papers.title: Establishment of a Common Marmoset Lineage Carrying a Frameshift Mutation in SETD1A, a Schizophrenia Risk Gene.
papers.abstract: Appropriate histone modifications are essential for maintaining functional chromatin structure and gene expression, and dysfunction of their regulators has been linked to a variety of diseases. Among these modifications, trimethylation of lysine 4 on histone H3 (H3K4me3) is a well-characterized epigenetic mark enriched at transcription start sites of actively transcribed genes. H3K4me3 regulates gene transcription by recruiting transcription factors, facilitating chromatin accessibility, and preventing DNA methylation. In mammals, methylation of H3K4 is catalyzed by a family of histone methylt
papers.summary: This study establishes a common marmoset lineage carrying a frameshift mutation in SETD1A, a gene encoding a histone H3K4 methyltransferase that is a known risk factor for schizophrenia. The marmoset model is intended to provide a primate system for studying how disruption of H3K4me3-mediated epigenetic regulation contributes to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric phenotypes.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer detection. It addresses limitations of prior methods that treat sequence and methylation features separately and struggle with low-signal liquid biopsy data.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new deep metric learning framework designed specifically for annotating cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data, addressing the lack of specialized tools for this data type. It leverages multi-scale information and provides interpretable results, enabling accurate cell type identification in epigenetic heterogeneity studies.

papers.title: Sotagliflozin, a Dual SGLT1/2 Inhibitor, Modulates DNMT1 and Class I/II HDAC Expression in Association With Anticancer Effects in Breast and Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors are increasingly recognised for anticancer activity beyond their established glycaemic effects. While selective SGLT2 inhibitors have been reported to suppress tumour cell proliferation and modulate AMPK/mTOR and PI3K/AKT signalling, whether dual SGLT1/2 inhibition is associated with modulation of epigenetic regulators has remained largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the anticancer effects of sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. Sotagliflozin reduced cell viability, clonogenic survival, mig
papers.summary: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, reduced viability, clonogenic survival, and migration in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. The anticancer effects were accompanied by changes in expression of the epigenetic regulators DNMT1 and class I/II HDACs, suggesting a link between SGLT inhibition and epigenetic modulation in cancer cells.

papers.title: Natural compounds as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers: From chemoresistance to precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Gynaecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial malignancies, remain major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality because of tumour heterogeneity, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. Epigenetic dysregulation, involving aberrant DNA methylation, altered histone modifications, dysregulated non-coding RNAs, and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) RNA remodelling, contributes to these processes. Direct evidence that natural compounds modulate m⁶A machinery in gynaecological cancers remains absent and is considered a knowledge gap.
papers.summary: This review examines how natural compounds can act as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers (ovarian, cervical, endometrial), focusing on their potential to overcome chemoresistance and support precision oncology. It covers DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, and m6A RNA remodelling, while explicitly noting that direct evidence for natural compounds modulating m6A machinery in these cancers is still lacking.

papers.title: Comprehensive epigenetic landscape of Sulfur Mustard (SM) exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.abstract: Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a potent vesicant chemical agent with profound and complex toxic effects. Traditionally, its toxic mechanism has been attributed to DNA alkylation-induced cytotoxicity and genomic instability. However, growing evidence indicates that dysregulation of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms constitutes a central link in SM toxicity, particularly in its long-term and delayed effects. Our study establishes an in vitro SM exposure model and employs integrated multi-omics profiling-including six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and non-coding RNA analyses-to s
papers.summary: This study builds an in vitro model of sulfur mustard exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes and profiles six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomes, and non-coding RNAs to map the epigenetic response. The integrated multi-omics landscape reveals that epigenetic dysregulation, beyond DNA alkylation, is a central component of sulfur mustard toxicity and may explain its long-term effects.

papers.title: DiffMethylTools: a toolbox for the detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic mechanism, and its significant changes (i.e., differential methylation) regulate gene expression, cell-type specification, and disease progression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Differential methylation has traditionally been detected by statistical comparison of two groups using existing tools and has supported a wide range of downstream analyses in human disease studies. However, few toolboxes efficiently integrate robust detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation, and the reproducibility of detected signals
papers.summary: DiffMethylTools is a new software toolbox that integrates the detection, annotation, and visualization of differential DNA methylation from bisulfite sequencing data. It aims to streamline the analysis workflow and improve reproducibility of differential methylation signals compared to using separate, disconnected tools.

papers.title: Identification of rare maternal copy number variants by genome-wide analysis of noninvasive prenatal screening data in 113,017 pregnant women.
papers.abstract: Knowledge of copy number variants (CNVs) is relevant to maternal and fetal health and can be obtained from noninvasive prenatal screening (NIPS) of pregnancy. However, genome-wide analysis of maternal CNVs using NIPS data has not been conducted in large populations.
papers.summary: This study analyzed genome-wide copy number variants (CNVs) in maternal DNA using noninvasive prenatal screening (NIPS) data from 113,017 pregnant women, identifying rare maternal CNVs at scale. It demonstrates that NIPS data, originally intended for fetal aneuploidy screening, can be repurposed for large-scale maternal CNV discovery relevant to maternal and fetal health.

papers.title: T-rex: standardized analysis of germline variants in whole-exome sequencing trios.
papers.abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) enables the identification of rare germline variants contributing to pediatric diseases. Trio-based sequencing, comparing affected children with their parents, is particularly effective for rare disease genetics. However, WES data analysis requires bioinformatics expertise, varies across institutions, and is often incompatible with clinical workflows. We developed T-Rex (Trio Rare variant analysis of EXomes), a cross-platform desktop application that enables the standardized and local analysis of WES germline Trio data without the need for programming knowledge. T-
papers.summary: T-Rex is a cross-platform desktop application that standardizes germline variant analysis of whole-exome sequencing trio data, allowing users without programming expertise to perform rare disease genetics analyses locally. It addresses the variability and bioinformatics barriers that currently limit clinical adoption of trio-based WES analysis.

papers.title: nf-core/pacsomatic: a scalable somatic analytic pipeline using PacBio HiFi data.
papers.abstract: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) HiFi long-read sequencing enables robust characterization of complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants (SVs) that are often inaccessible to short-read technologies. To fully leverage HiFi reads to advance cancer genomics and epigenetics, researchers require an end-to-end, scalable and optimized bioinformatics workflow. The nf-core framework meets this need by providing rigorously tested, community-curated pipelines that ensure reproducibility, transparency, and broad compatibility across computational environments.
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/pacsomatic, a scalable end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline for analyzing somatic variants from PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing data. The pipeline leverages HiFi's ability to resolve complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants that short-read methods often miss, with a focus on cancer genomics and epigenetics. Built on the nf-core framework, it emphasizes reproducibility, transparency, and compatibility across computing environments.

papers.title: ECHO: a nanopore sequencing-based workflow for (epi)genetic profiling of the human repeatome.
papers.abstract: The human genome is dominated by repetitive DNA, whose genetic and epigenetic variation plays a key role in gene regulation, genome stability, and disease. Recent advances in long-read sequencing now enable large-scale, haplotype-resolved, and DNA methylation-informative analysis of the human genome, including on previously inaccessible complex and repetitive regions. However, the comprehensive, simultaneous characterisation of the "human repeatome" remains challenging, largely due to the lack of comprehensive tools integrated in a single pipeline that can capture the full spectrum of variatio
papers.summary: ECHO is a new bioinformatics workflow that uses nanopore long-read sequencing to simultaneously profile genetic and epigenetic (DNA methylation) variation across the human repeatome—the large, repetitive portions of the genome that are typically hard to analyze. It addresses the lack of integrated tools by combining haplotype-resolved variant detection with methylation calling in a single pipeline, making repeat regions more accessible for study.

papers.title: Protocol for haplotype-resolved structural variant detection via long-read sequencing using cuteHap.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies have revolutionized human genome exploration at an unparalleled resolution, particularly facilitating the analysis of structural variation (SV) at haplotype resolution. Here, we present a protocol for using cuteHap, a robust framework for haplotype-aware SV detection through phased alignment reads generated by diverse long-read sequencing platforms. We describe procedures for single-nucleotide variant (SNV) calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping. We also establish a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate the detected SV callsets. For complete details on
papers.summary: This protocol describes cuteHap, a framework for detecting structural variants (SVs) at haplotype resolution using long-read sequencing data. It outlines steps for SNV calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping across multiple long-read platforms, plus a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate SV callsets. The protocol aims to make haplotype-aware SV analysis accessible and reproducible for human genomics studies.

papers.title: Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0, an engineered derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides, encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors.
papers.abstract: In 2016, researchers at the J. Craig Venter Institute produced JCVI-Syn3.0, a derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri Large Colony strain GM12 with a re-engineered, minimized genome. The minimal synthetic genome of 532 kbp encodes 473 genes, selected from ∼910 parent genes on the basis of their indispensability, that is, a lethal phenotype caused by a knockout of each such gene. Among these genes, 438 genes encode proteins, of which ∼150 were not assigned a molecular function or predicted cellular role. A decade later, despite community annotation efforts, 50-60 of these putative protei
papers.summary: This paper re-analyzes the minimal synthetic bacterium JCVI-syn3.0, whose 473-gene genome still contains roughly 150 proteins of unknown function. The authors identify previously unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors among these uncharacterized genes, suggesting the minimal cell retains more functional complexity than its stripped-down genome implies.

papers.title: Genetic variation in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways associated with prostate cancer susceptibility: a pathway-based analysis.
papers.abstract: Redox imbalance and impaired detoxification pathways have been implicated in prostate carcinogenesis; however, the specific genetic variants that modulate these processes remain insufficiently characterized. We used a two-stage, pathway-focused design in which PRACTICAL consortium meta-GWAS summary statistics (79,148 cases and 61,106 controls) were used for initial gene-level prioritization, whereas formal variant-level effect estimation was based on FinnGen and UK Biobank summary statistics (19,209 cases and 288,847 controls). PRACTICAL was not included in the formal variant-level meta-analys
papers.summary: This study used a two-stage pathway-based design to test whether genetic variants in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways are associated with prostate cancer risk. Initial gene prioritization leveraged PRACTICAL consortium meta-GWAS data, while formal variant-level effect estimates came from FinnGen and UK Biobank, identifying variants in redox and detoxification genes linked to susceptibility.

papers.title: Carbon substrate type shapes spatial self-organization in a multi-species biofilm community.
papers.abstract: Spatial organization is a defining feature of multispecies biofilms and critically influences microbial interactions and emergent community properties. However, understanding and manipulating how microbes assemble into spatially structured biofilms remains challenging because most experimental frameworks emphasize species composition and pairwise interactions, while often overlooking the spatial constraints on biofilms imposed by the environment. In this study, we focus on how carbon substrate type, distinguishing between diffusible sugars and polymeric substrates, affects biofilm self-organiz
papers.summary: This study shows that the type of carbon substrate—diffusible sugars versus polymeric substrates—strongly shapes how multiple microbial species spatially organize themselves within a biofilm community. The findings highlight that environmental spatial constraints, not just species composition and pairwise interactions, are key drivers of biofilm structure and emergent community properties.

papers.title: Pangenomes aid accurate detection of large insertions and deletions from targeted sequencing: the case of cardiomyopathies.
papers.abstract: Gene panels represent a widely used strategy for genetic testing in a vast range of Mendelian disorders. While this approach aids reliable bioinformatic detection of short coding variants, it often fails to detect many larger variants. Recent studies have recommended the adoption of pangenome references (as opposed to linear reference genomes like GRCh38) to augment detection of large variants from targeted sequencing, potentially providing diagnostic laboratories with the possibility to streamline diagnostic work-ups and reduce costs.
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether pangenome references improve the detection of large insertions and deletions from targeted gene panel sequencing, using cardiomyopathies as a test case. The authors show that pangenome-based analysis can capture larger variants that are typically missed by standard linear reference genomes like GRCh38, potentially streamlining diagnostic workflows and reducing costs in clinical genetics.

papers.title: Computational Pipeline Reveals Nature's Untapped Reservoir of Halogenating Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Microbial halogenated natural products (hNPs) hold ecological, agricultural, and biomedical relevance. The hNP-producing potential of an organism can be assessed by the precise prediction of halogenating enzymes, yet detailed annotations of halogenases are often missing from genomic and metagenomic data. We created a manually curated database (https://halogenases.secondarymetabolites.org/) containing information on the halide specificity, role, and position of verified catalytic residues and the results of mutagenesis studies of more than 120 experimentally validated or in silico inferred halo
papers.summary: The authors built a manually curated database of over 120 experimentally validated or computationally inferred halogenating enzymes, capturing halide specificity, catalytic residue positions, and mutagenesis data. Using this resource, they developed a computational pipeline to predict halogenases from genomic and metagenomic data, revealing a large untapped reservoir of these enzymes in nature.

papers.title: Ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry reveals EZH2-driven reprogramming of nucleic acid and protein methylation.
papers.abstract: ENHANCER OF ZESTE: homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, is a key epigenetic regulator frequently dysregulated in cancer. To determine its impact on nucleotide biosynthesis and nucleic acid methylation in intact cells requires highly sensitive, isomer-resolving analytical workflows. We developed a targeted ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution Fourier transform mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) workflow with lower limits of quantification down to 9 fmol on-column to determine changes in methylation of DNA, total RNA, and mRNA in A549 cells following EZH2 knockdown (KD). Usin
papers.summary: The authors developed a targeted ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry workflow capable of quantifying methylated nucleotides at femtomole sensitivity, resolving isomeric methylated species in DNA, total RNA, and mRNA. Applying this to A549 cells with EZH2 knockdown, they reveal that the epigenetic regulator EZH2 broadly reprograms nucleic acid methylation and also affects protein methylation, linking histone methylation machinery to wider cellular methylome dynamics.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings combined with genomic-neighborhood features and confidence-tiered neighbor voting to fill in missing functional annotations in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 metagenomes from inoculated and uninoculated silages, CAAC improved coverage of carbohydrate metabolism genes, achieving an F1-macro of 84.64% in cross-validation. This addresses a common bottleneck where unannotated genes obscure metabolic interpretation in microbiome studies.

papers.title: Identification of DNA-Binding Factor Enrichment in Chromatin Accessibility Data to Define a Persister Cell Signature.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-resistant persister cells are a major driver of cancer recurrence, yet their epigenetic basis remains poorly characterized. This protocol describes a computational pipeline for identifying DNA-binding factors (DBFs) that are enriched in accessible chromatin that collectively define a persister cell signature (PCS). Starting from single-nucleus ATAC-seq (snATAC-seq) data processed through the 10x Genomics CellRanger ARC pipeline, this protocol covers (1) the creation of a Seurat/Signac object with ATAC peaks, (2) the optional integration of DNA-binding data from the ReMap2022 datab
papers.summary: This protocol describes a computational pipeline for identifying DNA-binding factors (DBFs) enriched in accessible chromatin regions from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, aiming to define a persister cell signature (PCS) associated with chemotherapy-resistant cancer cells. It covers creating a Seurat/Signac object with ATAC peaks and optionally integrating DNA-binding data from ReMap2022. The approach provides a standardized workflow for linking chromatin accessibility to transcription factor activity in the context of cancer persistence.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Cross-Study Synthesis in Genome Editing: Comparing Long-Context Strategies and Uncovering Latent Contradictions in the CRISPR-Cas9 Guide RNA Prediction Literature.
papers.abstract: Predicting CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA efficiency and off-target activity is a precondition for precise genome editing. Computational models have progressively incorporated chromatin accessibility and epigenetic descriptors into their feature sets, yet synthesising findings from independently published studies-especially when those studies contradict one another-remains an unresolved methodological gap. Large Language Models (LLMs) have been proposed as a route to automate cross-study synthesis, but their utility depends on a constraint that receives less attention than model architecture: how much
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how well large language models can synthesize findings across independently published CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA prediction studies, comparing different long-context strategies. It identifies latent contradictions in the literature that standard reviews may miss, highlighting both the promise and the context-length constraints of LLM-assisted cross-study synthesis.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), a common diagnostic challenge due to overlapping features. The analysis identifies two methylation subtypes of MOC with potential prognostic relevance and reveals that mucinous borderline ovarian tumors split into two groups, one resembling normal ovary and one resembling MOC. These findings suggest DNA methylation profiling could improve diagnostic classification and risk stratification for these tumors.

papers.title: The LncRNA-Tumor Immune Microenvironment Nexus: Integrative Insights for Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as pivotal regulators of tumor-immune interactions, bridging epigenetic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional control of immune signaling networks. Recent multi-omics analyses reveal that lncRNAs shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by influencing immune-cell differentiation, activation, and exhaustion, as well as cytokine, chemokine, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Acting through molecular scaffolding, chromatin remodeling, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanisms, lncRNAs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics evidence showing how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate the tumor immune microenvironment by controlling immune cell differentiation, activation, and exhaustion, as well as cytokine, chemokine, and immune-checkpoint pathways. It highlights molecular mechanisms such as scaffolding, chromatin remodeling, and ceRNA activity, and discusses the potential of targeting lncRNAs to improve cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Integrated proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiling identifies SRA1 as a novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is among the most common complications of childbirth, and identifying novel treatments is vital. We aimed to identify potential drug targets for PPD by integrating the plasma proteome, transcriptome and epigenome. We designed a comprehensive analysis pipeline involving two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) (for proteins), colocalisation (for coding genes), and summary-based MR (SMR) (for mRNA and DNA methylation) to identify potential therapeutic targets for PPD. Genetic data on the plasma proteome were obtained from 4907 aptamers in 35,559 Icelanders and 7596 pro
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data using Mendelian randomization and colocalization approaches to identify causal drug targets for postpartum depression. The analysis pinpoints SRA1 as a novel potential therapeutic target, linking genetic variants affecting its expression and methylation to PPD risk. The work demonstrates how multi-omics causal inference can prioritize targets for a condition with limited treatment options.

papers.title: CUT&RUN as a Powerful Tool for Chromatin Profiling: A Focus on Neuropsychiatric Disorders.
papers.abstract: Proper regulation of gene expression involves a complex array of crosstalk between chromatin remodeling, histone and DNA modifications, and transcription factors. Dysregulation of these processes is implicated in a wide range of neuropsychiatric conditions. Methods to interrogate transcription factors and epigenomic profiles have revolutionized our ability to study molecular mechanisms in the brain. However, as our understanding of this highly complex system has grown, so has the need for more sophisticated methodology to disentangle such multifaceted and cooperative mechanisms. In this review
papers.summary: This review highlights CUT&RUN as a powerful chromatin profiling technique for studying transcription factor binding and epigenomic regulation in the brain, with a specific focus on neuropsychiatric disorders. It discusses how the method addresses limitations of older approaches like ChIP-seq, enabling more precise interrogation of the complex chromatin mechanisms implicated in conditions such as schizophrenia, depression, and bipolar disorder.

papers.title: 'PePApipe': A complete bioinformatics analysis pipeline for African Swine Fever Virus genome.
papers.abstract: African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) is of high concern in porcine livestock across the world due to both the high mortality rates and the trade restrictions imposed on affected regions. The viral genome is large and complex, and genomic analysis is essential for tracing its origin and evolution. Although several bioinformatics tools exist for genome assembly and analysis, no single platform integrates all necessary steps in an accessible and systematic way. In this study the authors developed 'PePApipe', a custom-built, user-friendly pipeline that enables rapid, complete, and efficient ASFV genom
papers.summary: The authors developed 'PePApipe', a user-friendly bioinformatics pipeline that integrates all steps needed for African Swine Fever Virus genome analysis, from assembly to downstream interpretation. This addresses the lack of a single accessible platform for ASFV genomic analysis, which is critical for tracing the virus's origin and evolution during outbreaks.

papers.title: Correlation assessment of SARS-CoV-2 variants and their subvariants present in clinical and wastewater samples in Oregon, USA (February 7, 2021 - February 26, 2022) using the Freyja bioinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance is a valuable tool for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 at the community level. As the virus diversified into many variants and subvariants that share overlapping mutations, resolving them accurately from wastewater becomes a key bioinformatic challenge.
papers.summary: This study applies the Freyja bioinformatics tool to compare SARS-CoV-2 variant and subvariant composition detected in Oregon wastewater samples with that from clinical samples collected over roughly a year. It assesses how well wastewater surveillance correlates with clinical sequencing data, particularly as the virus diversified into variants with overlapping mutations that complicate deconvolution.

papers.title: Complete Genome Sequencing of Occult Hepatitis B Virus in Hemodialysis Patients Reveals Subgenotype D2 and Immune Escape Mutations in Bangladesh.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health concern, and occult HBV infection (OBI) presents significant diagnostic and clinical challenges, particularly among hemodialysis (HD) patients. This study is aimed at characterizing complete HBV genomes from maintenance HD patients with OBI in Bangladesh to elucidate genetic features, mutational patterns, and clinical implications. Serum samples from two HBsAg-negative HD patients were screened by ELISA and quantitative PCR. Viral DNA was amplified by PCR across four overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) and sequenced on the Illumina platf
papers.summary: This study sequenced complete HBV genomes from two hemodialysis patients in Bangladesh with occult hepatitis B infection (HBsAg-negative but viral DNA positive). The viruses belonged to subgenotype D2 and carried immune escape mutations, highlighting the risk of missed infections and diagnostic challenges in this vulnerable patient group.

papers.title: Genomic exploration and in silico prioritization of putative COX-2-targeting metabolites from Streptomyces sp. VITGV156 (MCC 4965).
papers.abstract: Streptomyces species represent an important source of bioactive natural products, yet systematic genome-guided prioritization of metabolites targeting cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2/PTGS2) remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the biosynthetic potential of Streptomyces sp. VITGV156 (MCC 4965) using an integrated genome mining and computational drug discovery pipeline.
papers.summary: This study applies genome mining and computational drug discovery to Streptomyces sp. VITGV156, aiming to identify biosynthetic gene clusters that could produce metabolites targeting COX-2, an inflammation-related enzyme. The authors prioritize candidate compounds in silico, providing a genome-guided framework for natural product drug discovery from Streptomyces.

papers.title: Isolation, antibiogram and whole genome sequence analysis of Pasteurella multocida type A from layer birds.
papers.abstract: Fowl cholera (FC), caused by Pasteurella multocida type A, represents a major threat to poultry production worldwide. Detailed characterization of the genotypic, phenotypic, and antimicrobial resistance profiles is essential for advancing epidemiological surveillance and guiding effective intervention strategies. A total of 80 suspected FC field samples were collected from which P. multocida was isolated and identified through conventional culture techniques, Gram staining, and PCR. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method with 16 antimicrobial drugs.
papers.summary: This study isolated Pasteurella multocida type A from layer birds with suspected fowl cholera, characterizing the isolates through culture, PCR, antimicrobial susceptibility testing against 16 drugs, and whole genome sequencing. The work provides phenotypic and genotypic data on antimicrobial resistance profiles that could support epidemiological surveillance and inform treatment strategies in poultry production.

papers.title: Body Mass Index and Facial Aging: Mendelian Randomization and Exploratory Target Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Facial aging reflects genetic, metabolic, and environmental influences. Although obesity has been associated with older perceived facial age, the shared genetic basis and direction of the BMI-facial aging relationship remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to test whether body mass index causally influences facial aging, addressing the uncertainty about direction and shared genetic basis. It also performs exploratory target prioritization to identify potential molecular mediators of the BMI-facial aging relationship. The findings aim to clarify whether higher BMI accelerates or protects against perceived facial aging.

papers.title: The metastatic spectrum in functional and non-functional NENs: mechanistic insights from multi-omics.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are biologically heterogeneous tumors in which differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but non-equivalent axes. This review focuses on functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), principally gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic NETs, and critically evaluates how site, lineage, stage, tumor burden, genomic and epigenetic alterations, immune-stromal remodeling, metabolic adaptation, microbiome-associated signals, and treatment pressure converge on metastasis and recurrence. Apparent outcome differences
papers.summary: This review synthesizes multi-omics evidence on how functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), particularly gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic NETs, differ in their metastatic behavior. It argues that differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but non-equivalent axes, and that site, lineage, genomic/epigenetic alterations, immune-stromal remodeling, metabolic adaptation, and microbiome signals jointly shape metastasis and recurrence. The abstract is truncated, so the specific mechanistic conclusions are not fully stated.

papers.title: A MAGIBU-based model for pediatric and juvenile CNS tumors: an in-house epigenetic decision-support framework compared with online DNA methylation classifiers.
papers.abstract: Background: DNA methylation profiling is a tool that provides key support for central nervous system (CNS) tumor classification. However, diagnostically ambiguous pediatric cases may result in discordant outputs across classifiers. We developed MAGIBU, a cross-platform, projection-based framework that embeds individual methylomes into a fixed CNS reference landscape, ranking diagnostic entities by local epigenetic proximity to support clinician-led integrative diagnosis. Methods: As a proof-of-concept, we evaluated MAGIBU in eight morphologically challenging pediatric/juvenile CNS tumors with
papers.summary: The authors developed MAGIBU, a cross-platform framework that projects individual DNA methylation profiles onto a fixed CNS tumor reference landscape to rank diagnostic entities by epigenetic proximity, aiming to support clinician-led diagnosis. They evaluated it on eight morphologically challenging pediatric/juvenile CNS tumors and compared its outputs with established online DNA methylation classifiers. The approach is intended to help resolve diagnostically ambiguous cases where existing classifiers disagree.
